title: Serial returners
titleChinese: 快购时代的“连环退货买家”
paragraphs: We've all done it. We buy something we think we like and then change our minds about it. Whether panic buying, an impulse purchase or shopper's remorse, we're fortunate many companies allow us to easily exchange or refund items. In fact it's so easy these days that retailers are seeing an increase in a new type of shopper: the serial returner.

A serial returner is someone who buys items, often in bulk, only to return most of them. 41-year-old Hester Grainger, founder of Mumala Club, estimates spending £300 to £400 each month on clothes, but returning "around 80%", she told the BBC. This isn't unique. Barclaycard, which processes nearly half of the UK's credit and debit card transactions, says that in the last two years 26% of retailers have seen an increase in in-store and online returns – with the number of items being sent back up by 22%.

It's a problem for companies. Handling these returns eats into profits. Free delivery for the customer means the company foots the bill. Items may need to be repackaged. They are damaged - making them unfit for resale. Tony Mannix, CEO of Clipper, a logistics firm that handles returned goods for major retailers, said about 5% of them end up "being binned." Sometimes the fast fashion cycle has moved on. By the time the item comes back, it becomes a cut-price item on a reduced-to-clear rail - at further loss to the company.

Some companies are taking action to deter this behaviour. According to a BBC article, four in ten retailers now say they charge for returns to discourage the sending of non-faulty items. Online retail giant Amazon was reported to have started barring customers with too many returned items. This is something a study by retail management system Brightpearl found over half of UK fashion retailers would consider. And Barclaycard says a third of retailers have hiked their prices to cover these returns.

But Vicky Brock, director of data innovation at ReBound Returns, a returns management software system, believes this isn't the best strategy. Speaking in a BBC article, she says discouraging returns shows a lack of understanding by the retailer. Using data, companies can reduce returns by helping customers choose better. Some companies such as Uniqlo and Asos already provide a suggested size based on the customer's previous purchases and information on height and weight. Ultimately, she says, returns are now as much a part of the shopping experience as buying things, and shops need to take this into consideration.

vocabulary.entry: panic buying [ˈpænɪk ˈbaɪɪŋ] 恐慌性购买
vocabulary.example: Panic buying of essential goods often occurs before natural disasters.
vocabulary.translation: 自然灾害发生前，往往会出现生活必需品的恐慌性购买。

vocabulary.term: impulse purchase [ˈɪmpʌls ˈpɜːtʃəs] 冲动购物
vocabulary.entry: impulse purchase [ˈɪmpʌls ˈpɜːtʃəs] 冲动购物
vocabulary.example: The catchy advertisement led to many impulse purchases in the store.
vocabulary.translation: 这则吸引人的广告让店里出现了许多冲动购物行为。

vocabulary.term: shopper's remorse [ˈʃɒpə(r) z rɪˈmɔːs] 购物后悔
vocabulary.entry: shopper's remorse [ˈʃɒpə(r) z rɪˈmɔːs] 购物后悔

vocabulary.translation: 当她意识到自己并不需要这个昂贵的小玩意时，购物后悔的情绪涌上心头。

vocabulary.term: serial returner [ˈsɪəriəl rɪˈtɜːnə(r)] 习惯性退货者
vocabulary.entry: serial returner [ˈsɪəriəl rɪˈtɜːnə(r)] 习惯性退货者
vocabulary.example: Serial returners often buy multiple items just to try them on and return most.
vocabulary.translation: 习惯性退货者通常会购买多件商品，只为试穿后退回大部分。

vocabulary.entry: in bulk [ɪn bʌlk] 批量地；大量地
vocabulary.example: Restaurants usually buy ingredients in bulk to reduce costs.
vocabulary.translation: 餐馆通常会批量采购食材以降低成本。

vocabulary.term: debit card [ˈdebɪt kɑːd] 借记卡
vocabulary.entry: debit card [ˈdebɪt kɑːd] 借记卡
vocabulary.example: You can use your debit card to withdraw cash from ATMs worldwide.
vocabulary.translation: 你可以使用借记卡在全球范围内的自动取款机上取现。

vocabulary.entry: eats into profits [iːts ˈɪntu ˈprɒfɪts] 侵蚀利润

vocabulary.translation: 原材料成本上涨正在侵蚀这家制造商的利润。

vocabulary.entry: foots the bill [fʊts ðə bɪl] 买单；付账
vocabulary.example: For the team building event, the company always foots the bill.
vocabulary.translation: 公司团建活动的费用，向来由公司买单。

vocabulary.entry: unfit for resale [ʌnˈfɪt fɔː(r) ˌriːˈseɪl] 不适合再出售

vocabulary.translation: 已开封或使用过的商品通常不适合再出售。

vocabulary.entry: being binned [ˈbiːɪŋ bɪnd] 被扔进垃圾桶（bin 的动名词形式）

vocabulary.entry: barring customers [ˈbɑːrɪŋ ˈkʌstəməz] 禁止顾客（bar 的动名词形式）

vocabulary.entry: take into consideration [teɪk ˈɪntu kənˌsɪdəˈreɪʃn] 考虑到；顾及

vocabulary.translation: 快时尚周期给品牌带来了快速推出新款式的压力。
